memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The angel of the Lord called to Abraham from heaven a second time and said, "I swear by myself, declares the Lord, that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son..." - Gen 22:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God speaks again, and this time He makes an oath - the strongest possible confirmation of a promise. "I swear by myself, declares the Lord." Because there is no one greater to swear by, God swears by His own name and character. He is binding Himself, in the most solemn way imaginable, to keep His promise to Abraham.

Notice why this comes now: "because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son." Abraham's obedience did not earn God's love - God had chosen and blessed him long before, by grace. But his faith, proven in obedience, became the occasion for God to confirm His promises with an oath. Genuine faith that acts opens the way for deeper assurance.

There is a beautiful truth here about how faith and obedience relate. Abraham was justified by faith long ago (Gen 15:6), before he had done anything. But that faith was real, and it showed itself in obedience here on Moriah. As James says, "his faith and his actions were working together" (Jas 2:22). True faith always, eventually, bears the fruit of obedience.

And what security this oath gives! When God binds Himself by His own name, His promise is utterly certain. Hebrews points to this very oath to assure us that God's promises to us in Christ are unbreakable - "so that... we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be greatly encouraged" (Heb 6:18). The God who swore to Abraham has given us promises just as sure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does your faith show itself in obedience, as Abraham's did?
- How does God binding Himself by oath give you assurance in His promises?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your promises are as certain as Your own name. Let my faith be real, showing itself in obedience like Abraham's. And when I doubt, remind me that You have bound Yourself to keep Your word.
Amen.
